claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films and nanoribbons possess residual interfacial strain.
Grain boundaries in the as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi structures produce lattice distortions.
Residual strain and grain-boundary lattice distortions drive magnetoelastic coupling in these low-dimensional FeMnNiGeSi alloys.
Strain-mediated magnetoelastic coupling governs the magnetocaloric response.
Strain-mediated magnetoelastic coupling governs magnetic hysteresis during low-field cooling cycles.
Moderate post-deposition thermal annealing can relieve residual strain.
The annealing treatment can be optimized to avoid significant grain growth and phase changes.
Intrinsic strain alters magnetic-domain nucleation and domain-wall motion through magnetoelastic coupling.
Annealing-induced strain relief lowers the energy barriers for magnetic-domain switching.
Lower domain-switching barriers reduce magnetic hysteresis.
More reversible domain switching modifies the net magnetocaloric cooling effect.
Annealed samples will have a smaller low-field hysteresis width than matched as-deposited samples.
Annealing will produce a moderate change in magnetocaloric temperature change relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Strain-induced domain pinning causes wider hysteresis in the as-deposited baseline.
Localized strain can limit the magnetocaloric response in the as-deposited nanostructures.
Heat-transfer dynamics limit the useful cycle frequency in these nanoscale geometries.
The proposed behavior applies at applied magnetic fields below approximately 100 mT.
The proposed behavior applies near magnetic ordering temperatures where the magnetocaloric response is active.

contradictions.description: The predicted magnetocaloric outcome is only a non-directional 'moderate change,' which could include a decrease, whereas degradation of magnetocaloric performance is separately declared falsifying. Thus, some outcomes are simultaneously permitted by the prediction and treated as falsification.
